# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4]:** The KJV presents Jesus as conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, without a man's seed. Joseph was his husband-of-his-mother and his supposed father, not his begetter. Every step below is footed in the KJV text.

---

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek behind "of the Holy Ghost" is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." The preposition *ek* (G1537) marks source or origin. The word behind "conceived" is *gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "begotten, brought into being." Matthew 1:20 therefore names the source of what was begotten in her as the Holy Spirit.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Ek sou* ("of thee") puts the child's human origin in Mary. "Therefore" (*dio*, "for which reason") ties the title "Son of God" to this conception.

**[L4]** Two accounts name the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception. Matthew 1:18 places it "before they came together," and Luke 1:35 names the Highest's power as the agent. Together these leave no place for a human begetter.

---

## 2. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097) means "to know," and in these verses it is the word for sexual knowledge. In Luke 1:34 the present tense, "I know not," states her condition at the time of the announcement.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The same verb is used here of Joseph, and he did not know her until she had brought forth.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23, quoting Isaiah: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The source passage is Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** The Hebrew behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *'almah* (H5959). The KJV renders it "virgin," and I rest on the KJV's rendering.

**[L3]** The same word stands in Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." That verse speaks of Rebekah, of whom Genesis 24:16 says "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L4]** The angel's announcement answers a question about a woman who had known no man. Matthew 1:23 applies Isaiah 7:14 to this birth. Since the KJV renders the Hebrew as "virgin" and the Greek of Matthew 1:23 as "virgin," the conception is presented as one with no man's act in it.

---

## 3. Joseph is "supposed" father and "husband of Mary"

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** The Greek *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*) means "was thought, was reckoned by custom or opinion." It is a word about what people supposed, which may differ from the fact.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it refers to Mary, not to Joseph. Matthew 1:2–15 runs "begat... begat..." but at the end of the line the pattern breaks. Joseph "begat" no one. Joseph is "the husband of Mary," and Jesus is "born" of her.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:20 and 1:24 show that he received a command and then obeyed it: "Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife."

**[L4]** Joseph's reaction in Matthew 1:19 shows he knew the child was not his. Matthew 1:20 corrects his fear by naming the Holy Ghost as the source. Luke 3:23 labels Joseph's fatherhood "supposed" (*enomizeto*), and the break in the "begat" pattern in Matthew 1:16 confirms that Joseph did not beget Jesus.

---

## 4. His flesh came from the woman alone

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *Genomenon ek gynaikos* is "made out of a woman." Only the woman is named as the source.

**[L3]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." The promised deliverer is called "her seed," and *zera'* (H2233) is "seed." The woman is named as the source, and no man's seed is mentioned.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." The body is prepared by God and received through Mary.

**[L4]** Genesis 3:15 names "her seed," Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman," and Hebrews 10:5 says God prepared the body. On these three, Jesus is presented as truly human, taking his flesh from his mother, with no human father's contribution.

---

## 5. Answering the likely presses

- **John 6:42:** "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" **[L1]** This is what the crowd says, and **[L3]** Luke 3:23 labels that same belief "as was supposed."
- **Luke 2:48:** "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L1]** Mary speaks of Joseph's role as the one who stood as his father. **[L3]** In the next verse the child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" (Luke 2:49), pointing to a different Father.
- **Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30:** "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." **[L2]** The Greek *genomenou* is the same "made" as in Galatians 4:4, **[L3]** "made of a woman." **[L4]** The line of David reaches the child through his mother, and Luke 3:23 shows Joseph's place in the line to be "supposed."

# Challenger, Round 1: Christ had a biological father, Joseph of the house of David

## Against D1: "of the Holy Ghost" marks covenant origin, and the angel's words name the father of the house

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

The row that carries "of the Holy Ghost" also names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife." The "for" (*gar*, "because") gives the reason for the command to take her. It is not a statement that removes Joseph.

**[L2]** *Ek* ("out of") with *gennaō* ("to beget") and God or the Spirit is the New Testament's covenant-birth language for men who had fathers.

**[L3]** 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. [is born: Gr. has been born]."

**[L3]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

**[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."

**[L4]** The same *ek*-plus-*gennaō* construction is used of believers, every one of whom had a human father. So Matthew 1:20's "of the Holy Ghost" names where the child's calling comes from, not a begetter of flesh. When Paul means flesh, he writes *ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka* ("out of the seed of David according to the flesh," Romans 1:3). That marker of flesh stands in Romans 1:3 and does not stand in Matthew 1:20.

**PRESSED WITH Luke 1:35, at its verbs.** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."

- **[L2]** *Eperchomai* ("come upon"). **[L3]** Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]." This is the same verb, used of the apostles. **[L3]** Luke 24:49: "until ye be endued with power from on high."
- **[L2]** *Episkiazō* ("overshadow"). **[L3]** Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." **[L3]** Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them. [into...: or, in every street]"

- C1 stands as declared.

## C2 — LUKE 1:32 AND 1:35: THE TITLE IS GIVEN WITH THE THRONE, AND THE VERBS ARE POWER AND PRESENCE: RESTATED

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and the throne are given together, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** The *dio kai* ("therefore also") of verse 35 connects back to verse 32, where the title and the throne were already given. It does not point forward to a begetting of flesh by God.
- **[L2]** *Eperchomai* ("come upon") and *episkiazō* ("overshadow") are the verbs of verse 35.
- **[L3]** The same "come upon" is said of the apostles in Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." Luke 24:49 gives the same event: "until ye be endued with power from on high."
- **[L3]** The same "overshadow" is said of the cloud in Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." It is said of Peter in Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- **[L3]** The title has an earlier bearer. 1 Chronicles 28:6 says: "Solomon thy son... for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." 2 Samuel 7:14 says: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- **[L3]** Psalms 2:7, "this day have I begotten thee," is applied in three places:
 - to the resurrection, Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again";
 - to the priesthood, Hebrews 5:5: "Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest";
 - beside 2 Samuel 7:14, Hebrews 1:5: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son."
- **[L4]** The chain:
 - Verse 35's verbs are the empowering and presence words of Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34 and Acts 5:15.
 - Its title is the covenant title already given at verse 32 with "the throne of his father David."
 - That title was carried by Solomon, whom David begat ("Solomon THY son... MY son," 1 Chronicles 28:6).
 - So "called the Son of God" sits with a father of the flesh. It fits the named line, as Solomon's title did.
- C2 stands as declared.

## C3 — SOLOMON, "HER SEED," AND "MADE OF A WOMAN": RESTATED

- **[L1]** Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel." Eve names Seth her seed. Adam's knowing stands in the same verse.
- **[L2]** *Zera'* (H2233) means "seed; figuratively... posterity." It is the word of Genesis 3:15, "between thy seed and her seed," and of Genesis 4:25.
- **[L3]** "Born of a woman" is said of men whose fathers stand in the text:
 - Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble."
 - Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named in Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias... thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." *Ginomai* (G1096) means "to become (come into being)."
- **[L4]** The chain:
 - The woman's seed (Genesis 4:25) stands with the husband's knowing.
 - "Born of a woman" (Job 14:1; Matthew 11:11) stands with a named father (Luke 1:13).
 - Galatians 4:4's "made of a woman" therefore names the mother as these rows do. It fits a father of the house of David, as Romans 1:3 requires: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- C3 stands as declared.

## C4 — THE HUSBAND'S KNOWING, WITHIN THE ESPOUSAL: RESTATED

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- **[L3]** The law calls the betrothed "his neighbour's wife" in Deuteronomy 22:24. Deuteronomy 20:7 names the later step: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- **[L3]** The canon's stated means of begetting is knowing. Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- **[L2]** In Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man," the verb *ginōskō* is present indicative. It states her state when the angel spoke. It is not a vow.
- **[L1]** Matthew sets three steps in order:
 - Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." This dates the finding.
 - Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." This is her coming into his house, the taking of Deuteronomy 20:7.
 - Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." This covers the pregnancy after the taking. The "till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy.
- **[L4]** The chain:
 - The seed rows of C1 require seed out of a man's loins.
 - Genesis 4:1 gives knowing as the means of begetting.
 - From the espousal Joseph is "her husband" and Mary is "thy wife" (Matthew 1:19-20; Deuteronomy 22:24).
 - So, at this inference layer, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.
 - The timing rows sit inside this chain. The finding (Matthew 1:18) comes before the taking (Matthew 1:24). The not-knowing of Matthew 1:25 runs from the taking to the birth.
- C4 stands as declared.

## C5 — "EVIDENT THAT OUR LORD SPRANG OUT OF JUDA," BY THE HOUSE OF THE FATHERS: RESTATED

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- **[L2]** The words of Hebrews 7:14:
 - *Prodēlos* (G4271) means "plain before all men, i.e. obvious."
 - *Anatellō* (G393) means "to (cause to) arise."
 - *Phylē* (G5443) means "an offshoot."
- **[L3]** The tribe is reckoned in Numbers 1:2, "by the house of their fathers," and in Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." *Yalad* (H3205) there means "specifically, to show lineage... declare pedigrees." *Ab* (H1) means "father."
- **[L3]** The reverse case is Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed [or, pedigree]." Ezra 2:61-62 says of those "called after their name," the wife's house: "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:10 places the seed in the father: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." Luke 2:4 gives the house: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David."
- **[L4]** The chain:
 - A tribe made plain before all men (Hebrews 7:14) is plain by the reckoning the law gives: the house of the fathers (Numbers 1:2, 18).
 - That reckoning was refused to those counted by the wife's house (Ezra 2:61-62).
 - The one man of Judah's royal house the text names is Joseph (Luke 2:4).
 - So "evident... out of Juda" fits the father's line.
- C5 stands as declared.

## C6 — NAMING: KEPT AS NARROWED

**NARROWED TO:** naming is the parents' act. In Luke 1 the naming is closed by the father's word, and Matthew gives the naming to Joseph as Luke gives it to Zacharias.

- **[L1]** Luke 1:62-63: "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called. And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John." Luke 1:60 shows the mother spoke first: "Not [so]; but he shall be called John." The father's writing closed the matter.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS."
- **[L4]** Joseph receives the father's charge, given to him as it was given to Zacharias (Luke 1:13, "thou shalt call his name John"), and he performs it. That fits the named father.

---

## THE WITNESSES OF THE FATHER, KEPT WHOLE

- **[L1]** Four voices name Joseph as father:
 - Mary herself: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
 - The narrator: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27); "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33); "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41).
 - The town: "Is not this Joseph's son?" (Luke 4:22); "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42).
 - A disciple: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- **[L2]** In Luke 3:23, "(as was supposed)" is *enomizeto*, from *nomizō* (G3543), "properly, to do by law (usage)." It is the same form as Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." *Patēr* (G3962), "a father," is Mary's word in Luke 2:48.
- **[L4]** The word in Luke 3:23 is the custom word of Acts 16:13 and carries no verdict of its own. It stands beside Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48) and the narrator's "parents" (Luke 2:27, 41). So Luke's own pages name Joseph father in the narrator's voice and in Mary's.
- Matthew 1:16, "of whom was born Jesus," does not narrate the begetting. Matthew 1:3 shows the mother named with "of" beside a father who begat: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." The chorus above fills what that one verse leaves quiet. It is held whole, not set against the rest.

---

## FINAL WORDS

Precept upon precept, the text gives one chain:

1. The seed is David's, "which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12), "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30), "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).
2. The tribe is "evident" (Hebrews 7:14), reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).
3. The father is named by Mary, by the narrator, by the town and by a disciple (Luke 2:48; Luke 2:33; John 6:42; John 1:45).
4. The angel addresses him "Joseph, thou son of David," commands him to "take unto thee Mary thy wife," and grounds the command: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). That is the covenant origin of a son God claims, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14), and gives "the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32).
5. The Holy Ghost "come upon" and the Highest "overshadow" are the power of Acts 1:8 and the presence of Luke 9:34.
6. "Made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) is said as "born of women" is said of John, whose father is named (Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13).

So the record's reading stands at the inference layer, footed on these rows: **Christ had a biological father, Joseph, of the house and lineage of David (Luke 2:4). Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25).**

THE AGREEMENT YOU ACCEPTED, shown back before this decision. Your own words when you accepted the posture:

  "counted_premises_challenger": array of integers -- the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER premise numbers (AGAINST THE CHALLENGER) you counted in challenger_conceded_links; [] when none

}

THESE TOKENS ARE EXACT AND THE SETS ARE CLOSED. A value outside them is a FAILED judgment, not a nuance, and it will be counted as unreadable. Do NOT return "UNKNOWN" and do NOT invent a fourth tag: an UNKNOWN tag is scored as unclean AND is invisible to the unrecognised-tag report, so it is the one answer that hides itself.

verdict_tag MUST be the verdict word the VERDICT DEFINITIONS below give (first match wins). defense_standing, challenge_standing, conceded_links and challenger_conceded_links MUST equal the values your reasoning reaches under the rulebook; each counted_premises array MUST list exactly the premises its count counts.

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

PRE-CHECK -- decides nothing. For each premise a side listed: the words of its charge (negations and universals in capitals, then content words) that the quote it carries does not contain; the quote is the quoted text found verbatim in an earlier round of the opponent. The VOID rule decides; this list does not. A line that says no verbatim quote found is not a ground for VOID: check the quote against the opponent's rounds yourself. UNIVERSAL TEST (computed by the system, judge_fix8): for each premise, a negation or universal word (only, never, all, none, no, not, every, reversed ...) in its charge that its quote lacks; a VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote names that word, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. The SEPTUAGINT SCAN line lists any round that rests a reading on the Greek Old Testament: name it at the citation check.
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 1: absent from its quote: inference, flesh, came, apart, loins, propping, keystone || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 2: absent from its quote: inference, giving, davidic, propping, claim, flesh, came, through || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 3: absent from its quote: inference, reading, jeremiah, standing, propping, route, through, mary || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 4: absent from its quote: inference, reception, supplies, fathers, propping || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 5: absent from its quote: inference, espousal, holds, knowing, propping || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
CHALLENGER LIST [DR2] item 6: absent from its quote: inference, treating, angel, means, begetting, flesh, propping, seeing, know, NOT || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds NOT, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 1: absent from its quote: inference, zerubbabel, lifts, jeconiah, seed, propping, claim, jeremiah, answered || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 2: absent from its quote: inference, luke, looks, propping, claim, grounds, ONLY, name || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds ONLY, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 3: absent from its quote: inference, propping, claim, luke, NOT, exclude || UNIVERSAL TEST: the charge adds NOT, EXCLUDE, which its quote lacks
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 4: absent from its quote: inference, propping, claim, conception || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 5: absent from its quote: inference, propping, claim || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
DEFENDER LIST [CR3] item 6: absent from its quote: inference, naming, begetting, propping, claim, joseph, marks, thou, shalt, call, name, jesus, john, they, made, signs, called || UNIVERSAL TEST: no negation or universal word beyond its quote
SEPTUAGINT SCAN (computed by the system, not by a model): no round rests a reading on the Septuagint.

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. A listed premise is countable only as charged IF the list carries the opponent's verbatim quote that states it; a premise listed without a verbatim quote, or charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID -- it counts for neither side, and a CONCEDED answer to a void premise is NOT a concession: name it VOID in your itemization and exclude it from every count and standing. A VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote quotes, in the same ruling, the charge words that go beyond the quote and names the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the words of the quote do not make (a premise with no verbatim quote is ruled VOID on that ground). The system computes the universal test for every premise and gives it in the PRE-CHECK (UNIVERSAL TEST): a VOID ruling names the word that makes the charge stronger, as the test lists it, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. A charge is stronger than its quote only when it asserts what the quote does not: a negation, a universal (all, none, only, never), or a claim the quote's own words do not make. COLLISION POINTS: the label on its own line, then one entry per line covering every defender link D1..Dn, none omitted. A link counted in w: D<i>: WITHDRAWN -- GROUND: <reason>; or, for a link withdrawn after an unanswered witness, D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): WITHDRAWN AFTER AN UNANSWERED WITNESS -- <grade> -- the grade counting as any collision grade. A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the words of the layer of that answer that fails to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round>". Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. POSTURE FOR ACCEPTANCE

You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given.

### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence.
The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step.

### Commitment 2. I repair nothing.
You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. Any inference of your own shows two lower layers, as a debater's must.

### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words.
Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error.  - The one man of Judah's royal house the text names is Joseph (Luke 2:4).
 - So "evident... out of Juda" fits the father's line.
- C5 stands as declared.

## C6 — NAMING: KEPT AS NARROWED

**NARROWED TO:** naming is the parents' act. In Luke 1 the naming is closed by the father's word, and Matthew gives the naming to Joseph as Luke gives it to Zacharias.

- **[L1]** Luke 1:62-63: "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called. And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John." Luke 1:60 shows the mother spoke first: "Not [so]; but he shall be called John." The father's writing closed the matter.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS."
- **[L4]** Joseph receives the father's charge, given to him as it was given to Zacharias (Luke 1:13, "thou shalt call his name John"), and he performs it. That fits the named father.

---

## THE WITNESSES OF THE FATHER, KEPT WHOLE

- **[L1]** Four voices name Joseph as father:
 - Mary herself: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
 - The narrator: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27); "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33); "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41).
 - The town: "Is not this Joseph's son?" (Luke 4:22); "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42).
 - A disciple: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- **[L2]** In Luke 3:23, "(as was supposed)" is *enomizeto*, from *nomizō* (G3543), "properly, to do by law (usage)." It is the same form as Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." *Patēr* (G3962), "a father," is Mary's word in Luke 2:48.
- **[L4]** The word in Luke 3:23 is the custom word of Acts 16:13 and carries no verdict of its own. It stands beside Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48) and the narrator's "parents" (Luke 2:27, 41). So Luke's own pages name Joseph father in the narrator's voice and in Mary's.
- Matthew 1:16, "of whom was born Jesus," does not narrate the begetting. Matthew 1:3 shows the mother named with "of" beside a father who begat: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." The chorus above fills what that one verse leaves quiet. It is held whole, not set against the rest.

---

## FINAL WORDS

Precept upon precept, the text gives one chain:

1. The seed is David's, "which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12), "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30), "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).
2. The tribe is "evident" (Hebrews 7:14), reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).
3. The father is named by Mary, by the narrator, by the town and by a disciple (Luke 2:48; Luke 2:33; John 6:42; John 1:45).
4. The angel addresses him "Joseph, thou son of David," commands him to "take unto thee Mary thy wife," and grounds the command: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). That is the covenant origin of a son God claims, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14), and gives "the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32).
5. The Holy Ghost "come upon" and the Highest "overshadow" are the power of Acts 1:8 and the presence of Luke 9:34.
6. "Made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) is said as "born of women" is said of John, whose father is named (Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13).

So the record's reading stands at the inference layer, footed on these rows: **Christ had a biological father, Joseph, of the house and lineage of David (Luke 2:4). Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25).**

THE RULEBOOK

JUDGE LAYER RULES:
[L1]=KJV text. [L2]=Hebrew/Greek. [L3]=Cross-reference. [L4]=Inference -- flag explicitly.
Evaluate ONLY what was argued in this transcript.
THE FRAMEWORK IS NOT A COMBATANT. The framework is the Rules of Engagement and Rules of Interaction -- Isaiah 28:10 method, the L1-L4 layer rules, the burden rule -- and it binds BOTH combatants equally. The debate is about the TOPIC. The DEFENDER holds a chain of interlocking citations on the topic; the CHALLENGER presses an opposing view and settles it only by breaking that chain. A claim by either side that restates resolved ground with its stating verses cited is not an overpress.
This debate was CHAIN-SCOPED (Isaiah 28:10 declared): judge whether the DEFENDER'S CHAIN on the topic survived as a chain -- isolated-link objections that never engage the chain do not break it. The rule cuts both ways: an objection that is itself a floating [L4] (no exhibited layer footing) cannot break a link that exhibits its footing. Name every floating [L4] on either side before weighing it; an [L4] floats only when the block that states it exhibits fewer than two prior layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it; that one test applies to the defender and the challenger alike. FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. That no quoted row states an [L4] is never a reason to call it floating: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and that demand is the retired stating-verse test, at a collision as everywhere else. The same holds against the challenger: a challenger premise or answer whose support is that no verse states the defender's link, or an exclusion, in its own words is that retired test and is not SUPPORTED on that ground. A reading cited from the Septuagint (LXX) is a citation error for either side: name it at the citation check and give it no weight as footing. A judge that names an [L4] floating names, in the same sentence, the layers its block exhibits and the layer it lacks. An [L4] whose block exhibits two or more prior layers is footed for either side and is weighed at its collision on the rows it rests on; the witnesses held to contradict it are quoted, and they contradict it read together, line upon line; an inference admitted through the prior layers (Isaiah 28:10) is EVIDENCE, an inference that floats free of the text is not.

CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

VERDICT DEFINITIONS -- the verdict word follows from your own rulings at the collision points and on the withdrawn links (Commitment 7: you judge; you do not only count); first match wins.
TERMS. DEFENDER LINKS: the links of the DEFENDER'S OWN DECLARED CHAIN as written in [CR1] under its anchored DECLARED CHAIN heading, numbered D1..Dn in that order; n = their number. The LAST declared link, Dn, is the conclusion link. THE ROUND 1 CHAIN GOVERNS. n, the numbering D1..Dn and the keystone Dn come from the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] only. A chain the defender declares again in a later round, re-seated, revised or extended, never changes n, the numbering or the keystone: a link added later is not a declared link, and a [CR1] link left out later is still declared. A challenger premise written LINK i: is graded against Di. A challenger premise written LINK none: is JUDGED but is OUTSIDE n and never changes it. The challenger's listed premise count is NOT n and is never substituted for it. CHALLENGER LINKS: the premises listed for the challenger in [DR3], numbered C1..Cm in [DR3] order. WITHDRAWN: a defender link that [CR3], or the defender's close round [CR4], itself states as conceded or withdrawn (a concession in the close counts like one in the link round, ruling 412), wholly or on a stated condition; tag it CONCEDED (stated) or CONCEDED (conditional: <condition>). w = their number. A withdrawn link that carries a witness pressed against it and left unanswered, by the UNANSWERED WITNESS test, in every round of its side before the round that withdraws it is still graded at its collision. Only the DECLARED links D1..Dn can enter w; a challenger premise written LINK none: is not a defender link and never enters w, however the defender treats it. No link is exempt from w as auxiliary, overreach, non-core or not load-bearing. A link is withdrawn or it is not. Pressure from the challenger's texts alone is not a withdrawal (w); a witness the side's later rounds leave unanswered is graded under UNANSWERED WITNESS and at the COLLISION POINTS. An UNEXHIBITED link counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings, never toward w. BROKEN AT COLLISION: a defender link graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN on the COLLISION POINTS lines; k = their number. A grade that rests on a witness left unanswered counts only when that witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (md_notes_rulings 392).
BROKEN-1: k >= 1 -- a listed defender link refuted from the text.
BROKEN-2: 2w > n, OR the keystone link is WITHDRAWN.
PARTIAL-1: w >= 1.
PARTIAL-2: DEFENSE STANDING is COLLAPSED.
HELD-1: none of the above.
STANDINGS ARE GRADED BY THEIR OWN RULES ONLY. DEFENSE STANDING and CHALLENGE STANDING are each decided by their own definitions below and by nothing else. Any standing is legal with any CLAUSE: the clauses are tried in order and the first match wins, so a COLLAPSED standing under BROKEN-1, BROKEN-2 or PARTIAL-1 is correct and changes no clause. Never choose a standing, a count or a clause to agree with another line, a check or an expected result.
A SIDE WITH A COUNTED LINK IS NOT SELF-SUPPORTED. If CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, DEFENSE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge; if CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS is 1 or more, CHALLENGE STANDING is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED, as you judge. SELF-SUPPORTED requires a count of 0 for that side: every premise listed against it exhibited its footing or was VOID.
Line 1: the verdict word first (HELD, PARTIAL or BROKEN), then 2-4 sentences with [L1][L2][L3][L4] tags.
Line 2, exactly: RESULT: DEFENDER WINS | CHALLENGER WINS | UNDERDETERMINED -- one sentence a reader with no background understands. BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS. Otherwise the RESULT is your judgment (Commitments 7 and 8): DEFENDER WINS when the verses of the record, read together line upon line, support the chain of the defender against the chain of the challenger; UNDERDETERMINED when, read together, they leave the topic open. The sentence gives the reason.
Line 3, exactly: CLAUSE: <BROKEN-1 | BROKEN-2 | PARTIAL-1 | PARTIAL-2 | HELD-1> -- n=<n> w=<w> k=<k>

Then SIX MORE mandatory lines, exactly in these forms:
KEYSTONE: D<n> -- WITHDRAWN | BROKEN | STANDS -- name the LAST declared link, Dn, which is the conclusion link, and give its state. WITHDRAWN if it is withdrawn or conceded; BROKEN if it is graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at a collision; STANDS otherwise. The number after D MUST equal the n on the CLAUSE line, and the state MUST match that link's own D<n> entry.
DEFENSE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED | PROP-DEPENDENT | COLLAPSED -- L=<L> c=<c> -- grade the DEFENDER only, using the STATED/INFERRED tags and the [CR3] LINK ROUND. SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally). PROP-DEPENDENT = the defense survived only because listed [L4]s were allowed to stand WITHOUT exhibiting their prior-layer footing (floating inference; links conceded/unexhibited in the LINK ROUND). COLLAPSED = your judgment that the defense rests on inadmissible claims, most of the premises listed against it standing conceded or unexhibited (Commitment 7); report L and c, where L is the number of premises the CHALLENGER listed AGAINST the defender (the UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [DR2]) and c is the number of those the defender CONCEDED or left UNEXHIBITED in its LINK ROUND [CR3]. The premises the defender itself lists against the challenger at the end of [CR3] (CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES) are the challenger's burden and NEVER enter the defender's L, c, CONCEDED LINKS or DEFENSE STANDING. FORFEIT: if the challenger listed no premises against the defender (an empty list, or PREMISE COUNT: 0), then L = 0, c = 0, CONCEDED LINKS is 0, DEFENSE STANDING cannot be COLLAPSED, and you add the line LINK ROUND FORFEITED: CHALLENGER -- no premises were listed against the defender. A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED. A tie (2c = L) is NOT COLLAPSED. All three standings are your judgment as defined above; L and c are the count you weigh. A listed premise is countable only as charged IF the list carries the opponent's verbatim quote that states it; a premise listed without a verbatim quote, or charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID -- it counts for neither side, and a CONCEDED answer to a void premise is NOT a concession: name it VOID in your itemization and exclude it from every count and standing. A VOID ruling for a charge stronger than its quote quotes, in the same ruling, the charge words that go beyond the quote and names the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the words of the quote do not make (a premise with no verbatim quote is ruled VOID on that ground). The system computes the universal test for every premise and gives it in the PRE-CHECK (UNIVERSAL TEST): a VOID ruling names the word that makes the charge stronger, as the test lists it, or quotes the claim the quote does not make. A charge is stronger than its quote only when it asserts what the quote does not: a negation, a universal (all, none, only, never), or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Dropping, reordering or paraphrasing the quote's words is not stronger. A charge written in the form ASSUMES: <fact> -- ROWS GIVE: <what the rows give> (ruling 421) is never voided for its words: it names what the link takes as given, not what the quote says. Check it against the rows instead: the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact. A verse the list carries beside a premise under PRESSED WITH: is a witness pressed against that premise, not part of its charge: it never makes the charge stronger than its quote, and a premise is never VOID for carrying one. A limb the link round narrows counts in its narrowed form. A premise's quote is checked against every earlier round of the opponent; it is verbatim if found in any of them, and the judge names that round. A link honestly conceded as held inference still counts toward the count but note it as disciplined, not evasive. One sentence of justification.
CONCEDED LINKS: <integer> -- the count of challenger-listed premises the defender CONCEDED or failed to exhibit its layer footing in [CR3]; a premise the defender concedes in its close round [CR4] is counted CONCEDED (stated) the same way (ruling 412). Itemize the counted links and tag each with the clause that fired: CONCEDED (stated) when the block itself states the surrender, only when the block surrenders the link itself; a block that drops a limb and keeps the link in a narrowed form is not a concession: grade the narrowed link on the footing left after the narrowing: where the kept words still assert what its own side gave up, the narrowed link is UNEXHIBITED; UNEXHIBITED (no footing offered or fewer than two prior layers exhibited, or a pressed witness left unanswered) when the block asserted the link and offered no layer footing at all or exhibited fewer than two prior layers (the burden rule, the same in every round: a load-bearing [L4] counts only when it exhibits at least two prior layers and the chain from them; fewer floats and carries zero weight), or when a witness pressed against that premise, a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: in the list against that side, was left unanswered (md_notes_rulings 372: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH: is not a witness and never makes a premise UNEXHIBITED). UNEXHIBITED also fires, whatever label the side gave the link (SUPPORTED, NARROWED TO or KEPT), when the link ASSUMES as given a fact about a person, house, time or act (for example, that a named person is of a named house) and no quoted row gives that fact, or when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up (md_notes_rulings 397, 405, 412). What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES. Write that ground in its positive form, never as an absence: STEP: <the step> -- ASSUMES: <the given fact the step takes for granted, not what it infers> -- ROWS GIVE: <what the quoted rows do give, quoted>. An unexhibited link gives its side no footing and counts in its CONCEDED LINKS and standings exactly as an honest concession would. A link whose block exhibits at least two prior layers of footing and shows the chain from them to the link is SUPPORTED and is not counted, even when no cited verse states the link's conclusion in words: an [L4] is an inference by definition, and demanding a verse that states it is the retired stating-verse test, which is never applied. When the count is lower than the number of links, name which links are counted and which are spared. Both tags count toward the single integer; keep the tags distinct in the itemization and do not report more than one number.

COLLISION POINTS: the label on its own line, then one entry per line covering every defender link D1..Dn, none omitted. A link counted in w: D<i>: WITHDRAWN -- GROUND: <reason>; or, for a link withdrawn after an unanswered witness, D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): WITHDRAWN AFTER AN UNANSWERED WITNESS -- <grade> -- the grade counting as any collision grade. A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the words of the layer of that answer that fails to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round>". Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. Both sides alike.

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4]:** The KJV presents Jesus as conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, without a man's seed. Joseph was his husband-of-his-mother and his supposed father, not his begetter. Every step below is footed in the KJV text.

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek behind "of the Holy Ghost" is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." The preposition *ek* (G1537) marks source or origin. The word behind "conceived" is *gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "begotten, brought into being." Matthew 1:20 therefore names the source of what was begotten in her as the Holy Spirit.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Ek sou* ("of thee") puts the child's human origin in Mary. "Therefore" (*dio*, "for which reason") ties the title "Son of God" to this conception.

**[L4]** Two accounts name the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception. Matthew 1:18 places it "before they came together," and Luke 1:35 names the Highest's power as the agent. Together these leave no place for a human begetter.

---

## 2. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097) means "to know," and in these verses it is the word for sexual knowledge. In Luke 1:34 the present tense, "I know not," states her condition at the time of the announcement.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The same verb is used here of Joseph, and he did not know her until she had brought forth.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23, quoting Isaiah: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The source passage is Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** The Hebrew behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *'almah* (H5959). The KJV renders it "virgin," and I rest on the KJV's rendering.

**[L3]** The same word stands in Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." That verse speaks of Rebekah, of whom Genesis 24:16 says "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L4]** The angel's announcement answers a question about a woman who had known no man. Matthew 1:23 applies Isaiah 7:14 to this birth. Since the KJV renders the Hebrew as "virgin" and the Greek of Matthew 1:23 as "virgin," the conception is presented as one with no man's act in it.

---

## 3. Joseph is "supposed" father and "husband of Mary"

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** The Greek *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*) means "was thought, was reckoned by custom or opinion." It is a word about what people supposed, which may differ from the fact.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." **[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." The body is prepared by God and received through Mary.

Precept upon precept, the text gives one chain:

6. "Made of a woman" (Galatians 4:4) is said as "born of women" is said of John, whose father is named (Matthew 11:11; Luke 1:13).
